items.page_title: Crypto Magnata — V39.0 Domino Master Club
tells: The dashboard displays R$10,000. The scan caught it asking CoinGecko for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP prices in reais and dollars. That request can explain a convincing live ticker. It contains no account identifier and says nothing about who owns the displayed balance.

Two claims appear side by side. You can check the market price against another exchange. Checking a personal balance takes an account statement or a transaction you can independently verify. The countdown supplies neither.
urlscan gave this visit no classification. The record supports a dashboard using public price data. It leaves deposits, withdrawals and ownership of the funds unverified.
items.critic_note: Give me ten minutes in The Sims and I can build their entire Executive Suite. Give me eleven and I’ll move the bed away from the fireplace.

tells: The browser title says “CodePen Demo,” and the scan lists assets from CodePen. The single recorded external link goes to Google Maps. Those details fit an invitation built from a template, down to the directions guests would need.

The interesting question is what happens at “Confirmar.” A picture of an RSVP button can’t tell us which fields open or who receives a reply. The scan provides no example of a guest being asked for credentials.

urlscan gave this visit no classification. If the invitation arrived unexpectedly, the host can confirm it through a contact you already have. The template title alone is thin grounds for accusing anyone.
items.critic_note: Breaking: the giant metallic 15 eclipses Maria Clara on her own invitation.

tells: The scanner started on a pages[.]dev address and ended on www[.]facebook[.]com. The page history records both locations, and the final IP belongs to Facebook. The screenshot shows the password field at that destination.

To establish a counterfeit login here, we would need evidence of a form on the intermediary or a submission sent elsewhere. The screenshot supplies neither. The record also leaves open why the first page forwarded this visit.
urlscan gave this visit no classification. If the link came with a story about your account, open Facebook yourself and check whether the same request appears there.
items.critic_note: All these people showed up to watch me forget my password.

items.page_title: Nedrivning København & Sjælland | Nedrivningsfirma med fast pris
tells: The free-quote button invites you to share details about your property. The scan followed gonedrivning[.]pages[.]dev from HTTP to HTTPS on the same host. That establishes where the offer appeared while leaving the contractor’s identity open.

The scan lists a Google Maps link labeled as a 5.0 review and links to four social platforms. Anyone can link to an existing business profile. A stronger check runs in the other direction: does an independently located business listing send customers to this quote page?

urlscan gave this visit no classification. The record shows the offer and the links. It doesn’t show who received a quote request or took a deposit. Before sending a home address, call the contractor using a number found independently.
items.critic_note: I clicked ‘free quote.’ Can you ask him to put the kitchen back?

tells: The game credits give us something to check beyond the horns. The scan lists a link to SalvatorePreviti/js13k-2022 on GitHub and a separate music credit. The Play, Restart and movement controls fit the same explanation: this page presents a browser game.

Credits can travel with a copied game. They give us a lead about its origin while leaving open who put this copy on EdgeOne. The opening screen asks the player to move souls. It shows no sign-in or payment request.
urlscan gave this visit no classification. A phishing claim would need more evidence, such as a later screen asking for credentials under a false identity.
items.critic_note: Lucifer lost a shipment of souls. Apparently the eighth circle is open, but Shipping and Receiving closes at five.

items.page_title: WEB SİTEMİZİN TANITIM VİDEOSU MUTLAKA İZLEYİN!!!!
tells: The school name appears inside a promotional graphic. A Blogspot post hosts it, and the scan records a request to code[.]tidio[.]co alongside the visible chat greeting. The school pictured, the blog publisher and the chat operator could be different people.

Loading a chat service explains how a greeting can appear without a staff member typing it. It leaves the identity of the person answering this inbox open. The capture shows no conversation requesting enrollment fees or student records.
urlscan gave this visit no classification. If the chat asks for personal details, check with the school office through an independently located number before treating a reply as official.
items.critic_note: “Hi there!” “Could you move two inches? The ad was mid-sentence.”

tells: The scan requested /favicon.ico. The HTTP history shows the same file path before and after the switch to HTTPS, and the server returned image/x-icon. The scanner retrieved the image a browser can display on a tab.

The report lists zero outgoing links. This visit never tested what a visitor would see at the homepage. A familiar graphic could be reused on a deceptive login page, but the image alone reveals nothing about where such a page would send a visitor.

urlscan gave this visit no classification. This is a useful limit on the whole exercise: a scan of one file can answer questions about that file. A claim about a login page needs a capture of the page itself.
items.critic_note: Gallery label: ‘Infinity, 32×32, with an unusually large black mat.’

tells: The screenshot offers an Allegro sign-in at allegrolokalnie[.]aukcja758487593[.]top/logowanie/48819. Read the hostname from the right: the registered domain is aukcja758487593[.]top. Whoever controls it can put “allegrolokalnie” on the left and a convincing listing number in the path.

The scan even found links going out to allegro[.]pl. A copied page can send its navigation links to the genuine marketplace while keeping the visitor on another domain for sign-in. Checking one familiar link could give a buyer false confidence about the form.

urlscan rated the page “Potentially Malicious” and identified phishing targeting Allegro Lokalnie. The branded login and the host mismatch support that assessment. The capture shows no submitted password. To check listing 48819, start inside the marketplace.
items.critic_note: Lot 48819. One used Allegro sign. Buyer must collect from aukcja758487593[.]top.

tells: The page borrows Ledger’s hardware-wallet branding. Its address, walletsupport-ledger-live-login-ch[.]vercel[.]app, upgraded from HTTP to HTTPS on the same Vercel project. Encryption takes the visitor straight back to the publisher who chose those reassuring words.

The page also loaded a Tawk.to chat widget. Pair a wallet-support claim with a chat box and a visitor has a plausible reason to start sharing account details. The widget is ordinary support software. It shows a possible channel for that conversation, while the transcript and operator’s identity remain unknown.

urlscan rated the page “Potentially Malicious” and identified Ledger as the phishing target. The brand claim and destination support that concern. The record contains no observed request for a recovery phrase. Use a known Ledger support channel and keep the phrase private.
items.critic_note: Somebody bought the whole bag of refrigerator magnets and spelled WALLET SUPPORT LEDGER LIVE LOGIN CH. Still had to borrow Vercel’s fridge.

rejected_log.reason: Human review caught '_phishme.com_session_id' cookie in scan metadata — likely a corporate phishing simulation/training domain, not a criminal knockoff. Excluded from the main aisle.
